prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map captures the enclosed 3D geometry of the vehicle cabin around the camera wearer, showing the wearer's left hand on the steering wheel as the nearest surface in bright white (~0.3–0.5 m below and in front), surrounded within arm's reach by the dashboard (~0.6–0.9 m ahead), the left A-pillar and side mirror (~0.7–0.9 m left), the overhead roof liner (~0.3–0.5 m above), and the rearview mirror hanging in front of the upper-right windshield (~0.5–0.7 m). Across the five frames, the camera wearer's hand shifts slightly downward (becoming partly cropped at the bottom edge in frames 3 and 4 before rising in frame 5) while the car turns slightly left and advances along the road. Unlike the RGB strip, where the upper cabin interior is lost in deep shadow, the depth map clearly reveals the continuous curved surface of the overhead headliner and the sharp depth discontinuity between the suspended rearview mirror and the windshield behind it. However, the map is unreliable for the exterior scene through the windshield, rendering the road, houses ~20–50 m to the left, and a pedestrian with a dog on the right sidewalk (approaching from ~35–40 m away in frame 2 to ~10–12 m in frame 5, facing sideways/away from the wearer with the dog ~1 m beside them) as uniform black except for a faint vertical streak artifact under the rearview mirror in frame 4.
descriptions.segmentation: In the RGB context, the camera wearer sits inside a moving car with their left hand gripping the steering wheel within arm's reach (~0.4 m ahead and below, partly out of view at the bottom edge), while outside through the windshield a road curves ahead with houses on the left (~20–50 m) and a pedestrian walking a dog on the right path (approaching from ~35–40 m in frame 2 to ~10–12 m in frame 5, ~1 m apart and facing away from the camera wearer). The segmentation map only detects the camera wearer's foreground left hand in frames 1 and 5—isolating its boundary against the dark steering wheel in frame 5 as a pink 'person' mask—which helps separate the cropped limb from the dark dashboard background. However, the map is largely unreliable: in frame 1 it mislabels the wearer's forearm as a 'dog' and splits the car interior and outdoor road into overlapping green 'car' and orange 'airplane' masks with an unsegmented black hole over the rearview mirror and houses. Furthermore, frames 2, 3, and 4 are completely blank, and the map never detects the distant pedestrian, the dog, the road sign passed on the right in frames 1–3, or the vehicle's mirrors and dashboard across the sequence.
descriptions.pose: Across the five RGB frames, only two people are present: the camera wearer (whose left hand and wrist are visible within arm's reach at ~0.3–0.5 m on the bottom-left steering wheel, partly occluded by the lower frame border in frames 3–4) and a distant pedestrian on the right sidewalk (approaching from ~35–40 m in frame 2 to ~10–12 m in frame 5 below the rearview mirror, facing along the path and not looking toward the camera wearer, with a small dog within arm's reach ~1 m to their right). The pose map is completely blank in frames 1, 2, 3, and 5, providing no skeletal tracking of the camera wearer's foreground hand or the approaching pedestrian. In frame 4, the map displays a single yellow torso-and-head skeleton tilted diagonally in the left-center windshield area, which does not reveal any true human pose hidden in the RGB image. Instead, this skeleton is a false positive hallucinated on the dark trees and houses ~25–35 m to the left of the road, while both the camera wearer's magenta hand keypoints and the distant pedestrian's body keypoints are entirely missed across all five frames.
